condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

L5 permeability records for rigid phenolic alkaloids and morphinans show high passive permeability and no P-gp efflux (C65/C74, same (-)-SPD measurement; C66 for GA2-50), indicating the query's phenol/amine morphinan is unlikely to be limited by gut-wall efflux.

The P-gp/BCRP efflux records for estrone and estrone-3-sulfate (C68, C72) involve steroids and do not establish the query as an efflux substrate; no L5 record provides affirmative hydromorphone-specific gut-wall efflux or intestinal metabolism evidence.

L4 human absorption records for close morphinan analogs show complete or near-complete intestinal absorption (dextromethorphan complete; codeine Fa 95% and >90%), and rat fraction-absorbed values of 0.92-0.99 for a polar morphine glucuronide support the absorption component of the high prediction.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability or matched oral/IV exposure measurement for hydromorphone under rifampin co-treatment.
No hydromorphone-specific fraction-absorbed, permeability, gut-wall efflux, or intestinal metabolism measurement; L4/L5 records are for close analogs or unrelated compounds.
No quantification of rifampin's induction of first-pass glucuronidation or efflux transporters on hydromorphone exposure.
Rifampin co-treatment could lower F, but no affirmative evidence indicates it drops below 20%.
